subject: general
question: A vendor bought lemons at 7 for ₹1. How many lemons must he sell for ₹1 to gain 40%?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Price ratio for same expenditure is inversely proportional to the **Quantity** ratio.

Cost Price (CP) percentage = 100% and Selling Price (SP) percentage = 100% + 40% = 140%.

**Price Ratio** (CP : SP) = 100 : 140 = 5 : 7.

**Quantity Ratio** (CP : SP) = 7 : 5.

Given CP quantity is 7 lemons, so SP quantity must be **5 lemons**.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 lemons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

Given → **CP** of 7 lemons = ₹1 | **Gain%** = 40% | **SP** of 'x' lemons = ₹1.
Formulas: CP of 1 unit = Total Price ÷ Quantity | SP = CP × (100 + P%) ÷ 100.
 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8f8583ea72f71e1d47f38bd3b6a5ed84f6903d96a8f2a31b5154225e2c74baa6.png] 
⇒ CP of 1 lemon = ₹(1/7).
⇒ SP of 1 lemon = (1/7) × (100 + 40) ÷ 100.
⇒ SP of 1 lemon = (1/7) × (140/100) = (1/7) × (7/5) = ₹(1/5).
⇒ Since SP of 1 lemon is ₹(1/5), the number of lemons sold for ₹1 = 5.

**∴ The correct answer is 5 lemons.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Unitary Method for Articles

Always calculate the price of a **single article** to avoid confusion. CP of 1 = Total CP ÷ Total Articles.

Inverse Relation

When the total amount spent and received is **constant** (₹1 in this case), Quantity is inversely proportional to Price.
